subject: ParcelFlow perf follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state, streaming needs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lee <sabrina@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: ParcelFlow perf follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state, streaming needs

Thanks for the convo earlier — quick recap and a couple of clarifying items so we can size Dedicated capacity and confirm SLOs. Key points from our call: 

- Target P99 latency: 250ms for streaming responses (end-to-end for first token), 150ms for non-streaming single-turn generation.
- Steady-state traffic: ~120 QPS, average 1.2k tokens/sec per second (across coalesced requests).
- Peak bursts: up to 450 QPS for 90s windows during batch processing/fulfillment surges.
- Concurrency: up to 6 active conversations per user, typical request concurrency ~2.
- Streaming: partial token output required within 80–120ms of generation start for UX snappiness; chunk size ~256 tokens.

Clarifying questions (items we promised to follow up on):
1) Tokenization profile: you mentioned an average token length of ~4 chars for your messages — can you attach a sample token histogram or the tokenized payload from last week's peak?
2) Long context use: how often do sessions exceed 8k context (rough %) vs being short prompts?
3) SLA priorities: is sustained throughput under steady-state more important than absolute P99 during peaks?

Next steps I propose: we prepare a short throughput-sizing sheet (I attached a template) and propose a Dedicated config (GPU type + pool size) and a canary plan for the first 2 weeks. If you can drop the token sample and confirm % of long-context sessions by EOD Mon, we’ll get a formal cost + latency estimate by Wed.

Attachments: parcelflow_token_profile.xlsx (sizing template)

Best,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — good summary. Two quick clarifications: 

- Token profile attached (small sample). Average token length closer to 3.8 chars; about 12% of requests include long context (>8k tokens) but those are offline analyst queries, not front-line UI flows.
- Peak bursts: the 450 QPS number is accurate but only for ~60–90s and typically happens twice per day around batch reconciliation windows.
- Streaming: primary UX path is our mobile app; we need first partial token within 120ms. Full output can stream for up to 6s for longer responses.

I attached the token sample and a short log excerpt — please treat logs as PII-redacted. If you need a larger sample I can ask SRE to export a 24-hr window.

Best,

Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ParcelFlow perf follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state, streaming needs

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Sabrina's note and sample. Quick internal take:

- Inputs: steady 120 QPS, avg 1.2k tokens/sec, peaks 450 QPS for ~90s twice/day, ~12% long context but not latency-sensitive UI. Streaming requirement: first partial token <=120ms.
- Assumptions for sizing: use a 4-context-window optimized model (quantized) for UI flows; route long-context analyst queries to a larger 32k model with different pool (offline, lower SLO).

Preliminary sizing suggestion (high level):
- Dedicated pool A (UI): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, continuous autoscale + 2 burst machines. Estimated steady throughput headroom ~160 QPS; peak headroom with burst ~480 QPS. P99 streaming ~200–260ms depending on chunking and kernel choices.
- Dedicated pool B (analyst): 1x A100-equivalent, batched, relaxed P99 (1–2s) for long contexts.

I'll prepare a formal estimate and cost delta for the Dedicated commitment. Can you sanity-check the GPU counts and whether we should propose a 6-month reserved commit vs monthly burst? Planning to include fallbacks (hosted small-model) for extreme peaks.

- Aditya

----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lee <sabrina@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: ParcelFlow perf follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state, streaming needs — proposed next steps and sizing doc

Hi Sabrina — attaching our quick sizing write-up based on your sample. Highlights and proposed next steps: 

1) Proposed SLOs and routing
- UI route (low-latency streaming): P50 60–80ms, P95 120ms, P99 250ms (first token)
- Analyst route (long context): P95 1s, P99 2.5s

2) Sizing proposal (summary)
- Dedicated UI pool: 4x A100-eq GPUs + 2 on-demand burst nodes (covers steady + 2x daily peaks)
- Analyst pool: 1x A100-eq GPU, batched processing
- Estimated monthly cost delta vs hosted: ~$22k (depending on reserved term)

3) Canary plan (2 weeks)
- Week 0–1: mirrored traffic to Dedicated UI pool at 10–20% of production (validation only)
- Week 2: 50% rollout with real traffic + rollback plan to hosted small model for extreme peaks

Action items for ParcelFlow:
- Confirm whether you want a 6-month reserved commit or monthly with burst capacity (reply with preference).
- Share a 24-hr tokenized sample if available — helps us tighten GPU count and kernel selection.

Attachments: redwood_sizing_notes.pdf (detailed calculation), parcelflow_token_profile.xlsx (populated)

If this matches, we’ll generate an official proposal with pricing and SLA language and route to procurement. Happy to hop on a short follow-up tomorrow if you want to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
